To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the logarithmically divergently lattice integrals I(p,a) have the structure I(p,a)=f(p)log(a/M)+g(p)+O(a) with f(p) and g(p) being universal functions, i.e., the same for any choice of regularization scheme.

for the logarithmically divergents one-loop lattice Feyman integrals the universal part, which is the only part that contributes to the renormalization of Green functions, is the same for the continuum and the lattice.

for the class of logarithmically ultraviolet divergent one-loop Feynman integrands, the lattice integrands have a structure which is the same as that for the continuum integrands when the latter is regulated by a momentum cutoff, and the same structure when the continuum integrands is regulated by dimensional regularization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of one-loop Feynman integrands in lattice field theory and the implications thereof for lattice perturbation theory.
the study of Feynman integrands in the framework of lattice gauge theory.
the study of the asymptotics of the lattice Feynman amplitudes in a general setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lattice Feynman integral I(p, a)/log(a) is universal, in the sense that its limit for a→0 is independent of the lattice action and of the regularization of the continuum Feynman integral.

, for the one-loop lattice Feyman diagrams we consider, the renormalized lattice Green function is equal to the continuum Green function, with the same renormalized parameters, up to lattice spacing independent corrections which are of the order of the lattice spacing itself.
the lattice Feynman integral has the structure of a continuum Feynman integral with a cutoff in the sense of the above theorem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the lattice Feynman integral I(p, a)= I(p, a, M) can be written in the following universal and exact form: I(p, M) = f(p, M) log(M/a) + g(p, M) + h(p,,M), where f(p, M), g(p, M), and h(p,, M) are independent of the lattice spacing.
the structure of one-loop lattice Feyman integrals is essentially determined by the corresponding continuum integrals and is independent of the details of the lattice formulation.
the lattice regularization scheme does not affect the renormalization group properties of the lattice QCD action, at least at the one-loop level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lattice regularization of QCD is consistent with the renormalized perturbative expansion of the theory in the continuum limit.
the structure of lattice Feynman diagrams is essentially the same as that of continuum Feynman diagrams, and that the renormalization of the lattice QCD action is essentially the same in both cases.
lattice Feynman rules can be defined for logarithmically diverging lattice integrals in a way that is consistent with continuum Feynman rules.
